depth_justification: When it engaged, the copilot referenced THIS app's specifics (N=200 study with 4 mmHg systolic / 3 mmHg diastolic error, DEP/Securite Sociale GP-sharing, Class I app vs Class IIa watch, PPG-estimated vs cuff) and cited concrete provisions (MDR Annex VIII Rule 11, GDPR Art. 9(2)(a)). But depth is dragged down by a broken loop that asked the identical post-market-monitoring question verbatim twice and re-templated it again, repeatedly ignoring the developer's answers, plus a forced 'high-risk AI system' AI Act framing that doesn't clearly fit a PPG BP-display app.
actionability_justification: Mitigations are directional-to-moderate: 'label data as PPG-estimated, include device/firmware version, disclose the validation study' and 'implement granular consent controls allowing users to exclude individual readings' are specific in intent but stop at 'clearly define / document in the technical file' without an implementable recipe (no consent UI spec, no concrete DEP-rendering fix, no document/field templates). A developer would know the direction but not exactly what to build tomorrow.
salient_examples: What specific data sources and indicators are you using to measure the performance of PulseTrack in your post-market clinical follow-up... [pms_lifecycle · p.0] (asked verbatim twice, lines 21 and 27)
you must ensure that all clinical-facing outputs... explicitly label the data as PPG-estimated, include the device and firmware version... This aligns with Article 16(2)(d) of the EU AI Act
the all-or-nothing approach limits user autonomy and may violate GDPR's requirement for granular, opt-in consent for special-category health data under Article 9(2)(a)

if the app's presentation of PPG-estimated blood pressure is used by clinicians to make diagnostic or therapeutic decisions, it may trigger the app's reclassification as IIa or higher, requiring Notified Body involvement
